decisions.reason: The source establishes font sizing for the separate PowerPoint template; it does not change the visual formatting requirements for bullets in the Word templates.
PowerPoint font sizing does not alter Word table stability, column boundaries, or text-box overflow behavior.
The source concerns a new PowerPoint template design and does not change the Word legacy-content migration workflow or its stability standard.
The PowerPoint font-size decision does not change the Word requirement governing column containment during overflow or legacy paste.
The source neither changes the v25 ZIP package instructions nor explicitly requires the prospective PowerPoint template to be included in that package.
The source does not change numbered-list alignment behavior in the Word templates.
The PowerPoint font-size decision is unrelated to entering manual line breaks after pasting legacy content into Word templates.
The source does not modify the PBU prefix, Danish naming, or applicability of Word style names.
The customer-designed PowerPoint template is distinct from the specified style system applied across the Word templates.
Discussion of possible PowerPoint bullet counts and text resizing does not change the Word templates' Tab-driven list hierarchy requirement.
The source introduces no change to the supported Microsoft Word for Windows environment or the reliability standard for Word templates.
The PowerPoint design's placeholder-image question does not change the visible in-field placeholder requirement for interactive Word fields.
